resources.string: Apply and restart the tracking service
Stop Bridge and any other eye or face tracking client first. Applying restarts the tracking service, not the headset; reconnect tracking afterwards.
Tune it in front of a mirror

Pick a preset, save and apply it, then look in a mirror with the headset on. If a movement looks wrong, open it on the left: grey is what the model outputs, green is what the avatar receives, and the settings that change it are right beside the chart.

Brows catch up in about 0.2 s instead of 1 s, the jaw opens more fully while talking, the mouth closes fully at rest, a slight tongue shows, and blinks and wide eyes barely move the brows. Held expressions stay as steady as stock.

Changes from stock: brow Kalman share 60%, Q = 1 (Q/R = 10); composite w = 0.85, eye-motion hold q = 30%; raise/frown p = 2 at 70%; outer follow 40%; Wide link g = 0.15; Blink link share 20%; eye k = 14; mouth smoothing share 80%, k = 9, second pass 0%; log compression 50%; tongue threshold 0.35, gain 1.25, EMA weight 75%. Everything else at the defaults.

Every movement catches up within about 0.1 s, close to the model itself; half of the smoothing is kept, so small jitter shows while holding still. Blinks and wide eyes do not move the brows, and the brow tails move on their own.

Changes from stock: eye smoothing share 50%, k = 24; composite w = 1, eye-motion hold 0%; Kalman share 30%, Q = 1, R = 0.05; raise/frown p = 2 at 30%; outer follow, Wide and Blink links 0%; mouth smoothing share 50%, k = 16, second pass 0%; log compression 25%; tongue threshold 0.3, gain 1.2, EMA share 50%, weight 90%. Everything else at the defaults.
PICO\'s original processing, for comparison. Blinks and gaze are very steady; the brows take about a second to rise, the jaw opens less while talking, and a slight tongue does not show.
The stock defaults in postprocessing.h, identical to postprocessing-default.conf.
Uses the model\'s values directly, only limited to 0–100%. Use it to compare: if a movement also looks wrong here, the model itself is the likely cause.
eye.enabled = mouth.enabled = 0; the output is the model value limited to [0, 1].

1. Tap Balanced, then Save and Apply at the bottom. Disconnect Bridge and other tracking clients before applying.
2. Put on the headset, look in a mirror in VRChat and go through the movements listed on the left.
3. If a movement looks wrong, open it and drag the sliders as the page suggests; the green line changes at once.
4. Save, apply, and check the same movement in the mirror.
The movement is a synthetic example computed at 90 updates per second, for comparing settings; it is not measured on the headset. See the Guide for how time is handled.
The chart recalculates while you drag. Tap a value to type an exact number or reset that setting alone.

The horizontal axis is time; the vertical axis is how far the movement goes: 0% is not at all, 100% is fully.
Grey: the model's value.
Green: what the avatar receives after processing. The gap between the two is what the settings do.
Blue dotted: a related movement at the same time, such as the blink while raising the brows.
White dashed: with unsaved changes, the result under the saved settings, for comparison.
The readings under the chart are taken at the yellow dots on green; the model figure is the same reading on grey. How far the avatar actually moves also depends on the PC-side mapping and the avatar's blendshapes.

The charts are computed at 90 updates per second to compare settings; the milliseconds are not latency measured on the headset. What you see on the avatar also includes the camera, model inference, streaming and PC-side processing.\nOn the headset, coefficients are converted using the actual time between updates, so the same settings behave about the same at a different frame rate. The exception is a smoothing amount between 0% and 100%: at a higher frame rate it follows faster.

The stock coefficients use 24 Hz as the reference scale (Δt₀ = 1/24 s ≈ 41.7 ms). For each source update the module takes Δt between adjacent source timestamps, sets r = Δt ÷ Δt₀ and converts a reference share a₂₄ to a = 1 − (1 − a₂₄)^r.\nThis makes fixed-weight smoothing (the brow composite at fixed m, rest learning, the tongue EMA) and the Kalman steady-state gain independent of the source rate; adaptive smoothing depends on each difference and is only approximately independent; a mix ratio s between 0 and 1 blends linearly per update without Δt conversion.\nExample: a 60% reference weight takes 60% per update at 24 Hz and about 21.7% at 90 Hz, both with a time constant of about 45 ms. The movement charts use a fixed Δt = 1/90 s and first run 1.5 s on the starting pose so that smoothing and rest learning settle; the Kalman filter uses its steady-state gain. The panel does not read the device\'s current source rate.

Changes go into a draft first; the footer shows how many are unsaved, and the affected movements on the left are marked. Save writes the draft to the settings file. Apply makes the running processing use the saved settings; it restarts the tracking service, so stop Bridge and other tracking clients first. Reloading or loading a preset replaces the draft and asks first if there are unsaved changes. Tap any value to type an exact number, see its range and default, or reset it alone; percentages are entered as 0–100.
